chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said during the Farewell Hajj: 'Indeed! The Trustworthy Spirit (Jibrail) has inspired into my heart that no soul will die until it has completed its ordained provision. Therefore, fear God Almighty and Majestic, and be upright in seeking; and do not let the delay of any provision lead you to seek it through any means of disobedience to God. For God, Blessed and Exalted, has distributed provisions among His creation as lawful, and He has not distributed them as unlawful.

So whoever fears God Almighty and Majestic and is patient, God will bring him his provision through its lawful means; and whoever tears down the veil of concealment and acts hastily and takes it through other than its lawful means, an equivalent amount will be deducted from his lawful provision, and he will be held to account for it on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.الرُّوحَ الْأَمِينَ: The Trustworthy Spirit — a title of the Angel Jibrail (Gabriel), who conveyed divine revelation to the Prophet
key_terms.حِجَابَ السِّتْرِ: The veil of concealment — refers to modesty, propriety, and working within lawful boundaries
key_terms.رِزْق: Provision/sustenance — ordained by God for every creature
key_terms.قُصَّ بِهِ: Was clipped/deducted from it — a reduction in one's ordained lawful provision as a consequence of taking what was forbidden
key_terms.نَفَثَ فِي رُوعِي: Inspired/breathed into my heart — a mode of divine communication less than formal revelation (wahy)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about sustenance (rizq) at the Farewell Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Baqir (AS) from a teaching of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) given during his final Hajj pilgrimage, establishes that God has pre-determined each soul's provision in a lawful way. The Prophet warns against seeking sustenance through forbidden means out of impatience, teaching that unlawfully obtained goods are actually deducted from one's divinely allotted lawful provision, and will be reckoned on the Day of Judgment. The Farewell Hajj (10 AH) was the culmination of the Prophet's mission, making these words among the most solemn and authoritative of his teachings.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our copanions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said during the Farewell Hajj: ‘Indeed! The Trustworty Spirit (Jibraeel<sup>as</sup>) has Inspired into my<sup>saww</sup> heart that not a sould would be dying until its livelihood is completed. Therefore, fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and better yourselves in the seeking, and do not let anything from the livelihood carry you upon seeking with something by disobedience of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Distributes the Permissible sustenances between His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures and does not Distribute in a Prohibited means.

So the one who fears Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and is paitent, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Gives him his sustenance from Permissible means; and the one who tears down the veil and is hasty, so he ends up taking from other than His<sup>azwj</sup> Permissible means, there would be a reduction with him from his Permissible sustenance, and it would be Reckoned against him on the Day of Jugement’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and a number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from abu Hamzah al-Thumaliy who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The Messenger of Allah during his farewell Hajj said, ‘The trustworthy spirit has inspired my understanding that no soul dies before its sustenance is complete (depleted). You must maintain piety before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, be meticulous in your work to make a living. You must not allow procrastination to make you fall behind in the work for living. You must not work in disobedience to Allah; Allah, most Blessed, most High, has divided sustenance among His creatures in a lawful way. He has not divided it in unlawful ways.

One who maintains piety before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, He provides him sustenance from the lawful kind. One who tears the covering curtain in hastiness and takes it by unlawful ways, it is reduced from his lawful sustenance and he is held accountable for it on the Day of Judgment.’”
